date_source: page byline ("Feb 15, 2022"); arXiv:2202.07785 v1 submitted 15 Feb 2022 confirms it

reason: READ BEYOND THE STUB: the anthropic.com page is an abstract only, so I pulled the full FAccT/arXiv paper (109,886 chars). It does contain hard measured results the keyword filter would have lost — few-shot LMs on the ProPublica COMPAS task reach 63% accuracy vs COMPAS's 66%, with a Black:white false-positive-rate ratio of 2.21 when race is in the prompt vs COMPAS's 1.92, i.e. less equitable than COMPAS — but every model measured is Anthropic's own (ref [3] = Askell et al. 2021, Anthropic), so §1 drops it as a self-report. The GPT-3 / Gopher / Google program-synthesis scaling jumps in Figure 2 are cited from refs [11], [62], [4] and fail §2 test 1 as summaries of others' work.
